MAHALAGANG ABISO SA MGA MOTORISTA

Kasalukuyang nagsasagawa ng pipe replacement ang Maynilad sa Payatas Road at mga karatig na lugar. Isinasagawa ang proyekto nang paunti-unti (by phases) upang matiyak ang maayos na implementasyon at mabawasan ang abala sa mga motorista at residente.

Mga Apektadong Lugar at Target na Pagtatapos:
 • Payatas Road – target na matapos pagsapit ng Mayo 2026
 • Soliven Street – target na matapos pagsapit ng Hunyo 2026
 • IBP Road – target na matapos pagsapit ng Oktubre 2026

Ang mga petsa ay target lamang at maaaring magbago depende sa aktwal na kundisyon sa lugar.

 Asahan ang mabagal na daloy ng trapiko sa mga nasabing lugar. Pinapayuhan ang mga motorista na dumaan sa mga alternatibong ruta. 

Magtutulungan at nakaantabay ang mga tauhan ng Traffic and Transport Management Department (TTMD), Department of Public Order and Safety (DPOS), Task Force Disiplina, Quezon City Police District (QCPD), at Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) para matiyak ang kaayusan ng daloy ng trapiko sa mga nasabing lugar.

Maraming salamat po sa inyong pag-unawa.

data.raw_text:
Good Friday eve morning to absolutely everyone in X-land and beyond—except, of course, my dear old pals Tom and JB, who apparently thought "starting a fire" was just a fun metaphor for turning a simple neighborhood scrap into an all-out suburban apocalypse. Relax, folks, no actual flames were involved (thank God, because insurance claims for "idiot-induced chaos" probably aren't covered). This is another gem from the Throwback Chronicles, just like yesterday's stroll down memory lane. Buckle up for some 1994 nostalgia, laced with the kind of sarcasm that only comes from looking back at your younger self and wondering, "What were we thinking?"

Picture this: A fresher, less world-weary version of The Notorious Rissy B (that's Marisa, for the uninitiated) and I are blissfully minding our own business, basking in that shiny new-relationship glow where everything's fun and nothing could possibly go wrong. We're out in the hood I grew up in, chatting with the usual suspects—Jrock and Ron from yesterday's episode, plus Tom, JB, and Brian (Ron's brother, who apparently drew the short straw in the family toughness department).

Enter the drama: Brian had just gotten his butt handed to him in a fight with some dude from the rival neighborhood—let's call it a classic "L" for loss, because why not rub it in? But oh no, our victor wasn't content with one win; he rolls back in on his shiny new bike (remember the bike, folks—it's the real star of this tragic comedy). Bike Boy (actual name lost to the sands of time, or maybe I just didn't care enough to remember) challenges Brian to Round 2. But wait, plot twist! Big brother Ron steps up like a knight in shining... well, probably just a t-shirt, but you get the idea. They decide to duke it out at Gwynns Oak Park—once a bustling amusement park, now demoted to picnic central with a creek and a waterfall for that extra touch of "romantic" brawling ambiance.

So, Ron and Bike Boy are going at it like it's the Thrilla in Manila, except with fewer cameras and more mosquitoes. Ron's clearly dominating—because, let's face it, stepping in for your little bro is basically cheating—but then, in a move that screams "genius-level decision-making," JB and Tom decide to jump in and turn it into a 3-on-1 creek-side beatdown. Everything happens faster than you can say "bad idea," and suddenly Bike Boy's getting tag-teamed in the water like it's some twisted WWE splash match. Marisa, Jrock, and I are over here protesting like the voice of reason in a room full of toddlers: "Hey, maybe don't turn this into a mob scene?" But nope, deaf ears all around. Sarcasm alert: Because nothing says "fair fight" like piling on a guy who's already down and then leaving him in a soggy heap. Heroes, am I right?

But wait, there's more! Ron, in his infinite wisdom, decides to cap off the victory by swiping Bike Boy's prized new wheels. Again, the three sane ones (that's us) chime in with, "Dude, you already won—let the poor guy limp away with his dignity and his bike." Spoiler: They didn't listen. Shocking, I know. Bike Boy, understandably miffed, mutters something about coming back with his "crew" to settle the score. Ah, the classic threat that always ends well.

Fast-forward a few hours: Marisa and I are chilling on the curb outside my parents' house when a convoy of cars pulls up, unloading 20+ angry guys led by Bike Boy. They demand to know where the bike thieves are, but he vouches for us as the ones who tried to stop it. We honestly say we don't know, so they search the neighborhood for hours, find the bike, reclaim it, and leave—restoring "mostly normal" to suburbia.

Thanks for tuning into this latest episode of Nathan's Neighborhood Chronicles: Throwback Edition, where we've learned, that stealing never works out well in the end. Unless, of course, you're stealing hearts... but even then, watch out for the crew. Have a great day, and please, for the love of sanity, don't be a dipshit.
